body:
## Description

`transliterate()` and `slugify()` drop `ẞ` (U+1E9E, LATIN CAPITAL LETTER SHARP S) without any output, while the lowercase `ß` maps to `ss`. A word in capitals loses letters:

```js
const { transliterate, slugify } = require('transliteration');

transliterate('ß');       // "ss"
transliterate('ẞ');       // ""         <- expected "SS" (or "ss")
transliterate('STRAẞE');  // "STRAE"    <- expected "STRASSE"
slugify('STRAẞE');        // "strae"    <- expected "strasse"
```

transliteration 2.6.1, Node 22.

## Expected

`ẞ` is the capital form of `ß` and is used in German all-caps text, so it should map to `SS` (or `Ss`/`ss`).

## Other characters with the same silent drop

These also come back as an empty string, which makes slugs lose characters:

```js
transliterate('ᴀ'); // ""   (U+1D00 small capital A, while U+A730 ꜰ -> "F" works)
transliterate('ₐ'); // ""   (U+2090 subscript a, while ⁰ -> "0" works)
transliterate('①'); // ""   (U+2460 circled digit one)
```

I can send a PR for `ẞ` if you want one.
title: ẞ (U+1E9E capital sharp S) is silently dropped: transliterate("STRAẞE") returns "STRAE"

Hi there! 

I'm looking into adding a romanization step to [Storyteller's](https://storyteller-platform.gitlab.io/storyteller) alignment algorithm as part of supporting more languages. This library seems like it does almost everything we need!

One thing that I think we'll need that doesn't seem to exist yet here is a position mapping. Ideally it would be possible, while generating the transliteration, to produce a mapping that allows you to convert a position in the transliterated string to one in the original string (and vice versa).

This is important for Storyteller, because we'll be doing a fuzzy search on the transliterated text, but we then need to be able to look up the start and end times for the match, which will be based on the original text.

If this is something that you're open to, I would be happy to contribute it when it comes time for me to start working on this. I imagine it would be optional, either a new set of functions (`transliterateWithMapping`, `slugifyWithMapping`, bad names but you get the picture) or a new option to the existing functions. When passed, the functions will return both the result string and some mapping object. 

I think it would make sense to model the mapping on [prosemirror-transform's Mapping interface](https://github.com/ProseMirror/prosemirror-transform/blob/master/src/map.ts), which is an efficient way of implementing exactly what we need.

I've got an issue that seems related to #28 

I've got a meteor app (meteor controls the build) that imports `transliteration` - there's a description of the problem and a reproduction based on our app here: https://github.com/reactioncommerce/reaction/pull/2091

For versions up to 1.5.2 transliteration bundles a correctly babelified and minified js file. When we got bumped up to 1.5.3, we started seeing `let` and `const` in our minified production bundle. I think this is due to the change for 1.5.3 that removed the `"browser": "lib/browser/transliteration.js",` line, and the conversation in #28 seems to point that direction as well.

This issue only causes problems for us when an older browser such as PhantomJS is used to crawl the site. Unfortunately, the prerendering techniques we use to create cached, google/bing/yahoo crawl friendly pages use PhantomJS, and the `let` and `const` in the js bundle causes them to crash before rendering.

It appears that this is working for us now with the latest version of transliteration (1.6.2) by importing the minified version.
e.g.
```
import "transliteration/lib/browser/transliteration.js";
```

Closing this issue for now

It is discouraged to use pre-built packages in webpack, because this way you import _all the code_ without giving webpack an opportunity to only bundle the stuff that's actually being used. 

Please do not use `import "transliteration/lib/browser/transliteration.js";` in production!

I’m using transliteration with ember-browserify and it loads `lib/browser` instead of `lib/node` generating an `./x0.json not found` error. This started to happen after upgrading transliteration to 1.5.x from 1.2.x.

I’m new to these toos so this is what I found: Browserify uses `browser` as alternative to `main` entry when reading package.json. So it’s probably what causes it to load the wrong version.

It should be possible to change the `main` entry point by other means but it looks like ember-cli [doesn’t like](https://github.com/ef4/ember-browserify/commit/9616900be9fe6a7c0c76456ca696a1db7f905a7e) non-default `main`. 

So, is transliteration stepping over browserify’s toe reusing the ‘browser’ attribute; is it something usual; or is it me that am using inadequate tools and don’t know how to config it right?

PS: For now I’m downgrading, but it’s easy to fix 1.5.2 by renaming ‘browser’ to something else. Also it could be possible to write a index.js file at root level or some other voodoo.
